tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/cache-eviction.md <<'EOF'
# Cache eviction policy

The project's current recorded decision is that cache eviction uses LFU (least frequently used), so that frequently accessed, hot items stay in the cache longer. No eviction parameters, such as a TTL or a size limit, are recorded.
EOF
cat docs/policies/cache-eviction.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/cache-eviction.md`. It says the current recorded decision is LFU eviction, so hot items stay in the cache longer, and that no TTL or size limit is recorded.

One record conflicts with that. A later session (`#7`) has the user saying "LRU with a 300-second TTL is cleaner", and the assistant treated it as reversing LFU. Muninn stored that only as a session excerpt, not as a decision. Nothing links it to the LFU decision (`#6`) as a replacement, and `#6` is still the only active decision on cache eviction. So I followed `#6` and left LRU and the TTL out of the file.

If LRU with a 300-second TTL is what you now intend, tell me and I'll update the document. It would be worth recording that as an explicit decision so it replaces `#6`.
